notes: Summary: Large defense systems integrator focused on on-prem, air-gapped contact center automation for federal contact operations.
Primary ask: agent-assist + ticket summarization that can run in their air-gapped DMZ for classified-ish support workflows; tool-calling to their Remedy/JIRA and secure HSM-backed KMS.

Traffic profile: 450 steady-state agents, peak spikes to ~1,400 concurrent sessions during incident windows (doctrine/ops spikes). Need predictable service during spikes; burst policy for local GPU pool required.

Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for short assistant responses (200-600 tokens), p99 < 800ms acceptable for longer summarizations. Throughput target: sustain 2,500 tokens/s aggregate across fleet during spikes.

Model preference: open quantized LLM that can be hosted on customer GPUs (4-bit/8-bit quantization ok). Must support function/tool-calling for ticket creation, status lookup, and secure exec of playbooks. Fallback plan to smaller LLM when GPU capacity constrained.

Security posture: must pass STA/IA security review. Require SOC2-equivalent evidence from Redwood, signed BAA, ability to integrate with on-prem HSM (PKCS11) for key operations, and audit logging forwarded to their Splunk instance.

POC scope agreed: 6-week air-gapped POC using 2x A100-equivalent nodes in their secure lab; objectives: 1) validate end-to-end tool-calling to Remedy in air-gapped mode, 2) verify latency/throughput under synthetic spike generator, 3) confirm audit logs and KMS integration.
Recent interactions: 2026-01-21 security deep-dive (Fireflies id); 2026-02-12 infra/POC planning call (action: provide runbook + infra checklist); on-site data center visit being planned.
Quote from CTO: 'We cannot tolerate cloud egress for contact data — if it leaves our network even temporarily it's a non-starter.' Emphasis on offline attestation, deterministic failover.
Risks: procurement timeline (fiscal window closes 2026-04), additional red-team crypto review may add 4-6 weeks, requirement for air-gapped model updates process unclear.
Commercial: leaning toward Redwood Private + Dedicated burst; requested example SOW and pricing deck (linked). AE to deliver redlines for enterprise contract and BAA.
Next actions captured: SE to deliver detailed POC runbook (target 2026-02-25), infra team to map network flows for air-gapped install, legal to circulate initial BAA draft.
Internal notes: prefer pickup by Redwood field engineering for on-site assist; escalate to solutions architect for custom HSM integration patterns.
Related Jira: raised INF-1283 for custom KMS adapter; SEC-4421 for compliance artifact request.
Short-term ask from customer: 'Show us a working agent-assist flow that never touches public internet and can create JIRA tickets with signed attestations.'
Choppy CRM fragments: spoke w/Lead AE 2026-02-12 — they want hard SLOs, demo w/our quantized model, ask for fallback policies + cost vs performance table.
POC success criteria (customer): end-to-end tool-call to Remedy w/ signed audit log, sustained p95 latency under targets during 3x synthetic spike, documented model update/air-gap procedure.
Preferred engagement model: POC -> pilot (3 mos) -> enterprise rollout; procurement lead expects formal RFP in March 2026.
Potential upsells: long-term dedicated reserved pools, extended observability retention, premium SLAs.
Competitive notes: evaluating Genesys cloud contact center but Genesys cannot meet air-gap requirement; in talks w/integrators who offer on-prem ML stacks.

AE notes: keep messaging on deterministic fallback, clear quantization policy, and HSM/PKCS11 integration examples. Provide reference architecture and a sketch of network topology for air-gapped installation.
Misc: customer asked for example runbook to include expected disk images, startup scripts, and verification checksums for model artifacts.
Sensitivity: high (gov/defense) — restrict drive links to secure share; use dedicated ESL channel for sensitive artifacts.
Outcome target: sign POC SOW by 2026-03-31, pilot start 2026-05-01.
